patches.what: `inert` passed through a spread, as an empty string when collapsed
patches.reason: Upstream writes `inert={!isExpanded}`, which React 19 types accept and React 18 types do not, and which React 18 also warns about at runtime because it is not a boolean attribute. The site typechecks and runs on React 18 (the same version the app uses), so the attribute is spread in as `inert=""`: the DOM gets exactly the same attribute, the collapsed panel stays out of the tab order and the accessibility tree, and nothing is logged.

patches.what: vendored from card-18, the published name of the same block
patches.reason: @shadcn-space/card-21 is only served by shadcnspace.com, which is unreachable here, and its source is not in the project's public repo (card-18 is, in the same folder, with the same layout and the same default rows). card-21 is that file with the copy updated, so this is the published bytes rather than a guess.

The upstream block hard-codes "Others tools", the vendor's own name and its badge. Naming the columns is what lets the same block compare ResearchEngine against subscription research apps, which is the job it was picked for; the defaults still render upstream's own comparison.
The registry serves the file with CRLF; this repository keeps text files LF so diffs stay readable.
